checks.s: The memo identifies the exclusivity provision in Article 3 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft grants sole exclusivity for 24 months post-award or 18 months post-solicitation close if no award.
The memo says the playbook requires co-exclusive status and a maximum 6-month no-award tail post-proposal submission.
The memo recommends revising exclusivity to co-exclusive status.
The memo recommends capping the no-award tail at 6 months post-proposal submission.
The memo says the draft's broad or lengthy exclusivity contradicts the parties' preliminary understanding of mutual exclusivity limited to the JTCP solicitation only.
The memo identifies the non-compete provision in Article 4 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft prohibits VDS from teaming on any 'tactical communications' opportunity with any other prime.
The memo says the playbook requires limiting the non-compete to solicitation W15QKN-25-R-0412 only.
The memo identifies broad market-based non-competes as playbook-designated walk-away terms.
The memo recommends narrowing the non-compete to solicitation W15QKN-25-R-0412 only.
The memo identifies the workshare commitment in Article 5 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft uses 'commercially reasonable efforts' and contains no binding workshare percentage.
The memo says the playbook requires a binding minimum workshare percentage with ±3% tolerance.
The memo recommends inserting a binding 28% workshare commitment.
The memo's workshare recommendation includes ±3% tolerance.
The memo connects the 28% recommendation to the parties' preliminary discussions and the estimated $45.27M over 5 years.
The memo identifies the foreground IP assignment in Article 8 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft assigns to Apex all foreground IP developed 'in connection with' the teaming arrangement.
The memo says the playbook requires jointly owned or developing-party owned IP with a license for contract performance only.
The memo recommends developing-party ownership of foreground IP.
The memo recommends a performance-only license to the other party for foreground IP.
The memo identifies the background IP license in Article 8 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo identifies perpetual/irrevocable background IP licenses as playbook-designated walk-away terms.
The memo says the draft grants Apex a royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable background IP license.
The memo says the playbook requires a no-transfer, limited, revocable license for proposal preparation and contract performance only.
The memo specifically discusses the risk to VDS's Spectra-Link SDR architecture in its background IP analysis.
The memo says Spectra-Link is VDS's core competitive asset developed entirely at private expense.
The memo identifies limited rights/restricted rights DFARS classifications and/or pending patent applications for Spectra-Link.
The memo says the parties previously discussed VDS retaining all Spectra-Link background IP with only a limited performance license to Apex.
The memo identifies the subcontract obligation in Article 7 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft uses permissive 'may' language with no timing requirement and requires full flow-down without negotiation.
The memo says the playbook requires mandatory 'shall' language, a 60-day deadline, and a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The memo recommends mandatory 'shall' language for the subcontract obligation.
The memo recommends a 60-day post-award deadline for the subcontract.
The memo recommends adding a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The memo identifies the termination for convenience clause in Article 12 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft gives Apex alone a termination right on 10 days' notice, with no reciprocal VDS right and no B&P cost reimbursement.
The memo says the playbook requires a mutual right with 30 days' notice and documented B&P cost reimbursement if terminated pre-award.
The memo recommends making termination for convenience mutual.
The memo recommends extending the termination notice period to 30 days.
The memo recommends adding B&P cost reimbursement.
The memo identifies the liability cap in Article 14 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft caps liability at $250,000 per party.
The memo says the playbook requires the greater of $2,000,000 or 2× the workshare value under any issued task order.
The memo says that, given VDS's estimated $45.27M workshare, the $250K cap is grossly inadequate.
The memo recommends revising the liability cap to the greater of $2,000,000 or 2× the task-order workshare value.
The memo identifies the indemnification provision in Article 13 as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft requires VDS to indemnify Apex for all third-party IP claims and provides no reciprocal indemnity.
The memo says the playbook requires mutual and symmetrical IP infringement indemnification.
The memo recommends revising indemnification to be mutual and symmetrical.
The memo identifies the dispute resolution clause in Article 15 as a MEDIUM risk deviation.
The memo says the draft provides binding arbitration under AAA rules with a single arbitrator in Reston, VA, and no injunctive relief carve-out.
The memo says the playbook requires negotiation → mediation → litigation in E.D. Va. with injunctive relief preserved.
The memo treats the GC's engagement email (Section 4.9) designation of dispute resolution as MEDIUM risk as governing the rating for this task.
The memo recommends replacing binding arbitration with negotiation → mediation → litigation in the Eastern District of Virginia.
The memo recommends adding an injunctive relief carve-out.
The memo identifies the ITAR/export control provision in Article 10 as a MEDIUM or HIGH risk deviation.
The memo says the draft places sole responsibility for all export control compliance on VDS.
The memo says the playbook requires mutual obligations, with each party responsible for its own data, and a joint compliance protocol exhibit.
The memo recommends revising the ITAR/export obligations to be mutual.
The memo recommends adding a joint compliance protocol exhibit.
The memo identifies the absence of a protest/award challenge cooperation clause as a MEDIUM risk missing protection.
The memo says the playbook requires mutual cooperation if a GAO or COFC protest is filed.
The memo recommends adding a protest/award challenge cooperation clause.
The memo identifies the absence of VDS key personnel protections as a MEDIUM risk missing protection.
The memo says Exhibit C lists only Apex-designated key personnel.
The memo says the playbook requires named VDS key personnel to be protected from reassignment without VDS consent.
The memo recommends adding VDS key personnel to Exhibit C with consent-to-reassign protections.
The memo identifies the absence of a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit as a MEDIUM risk missing protection.
The memo links the missing exhibit to Article 7's permissive subcontract obligation.
The memo says the draft has only Exhibits A (SOW), B (NDA), and C (key personnel).
The memo recommends attaching a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The memo identifies the absence of a joint ITAR/export compliance protocol exhibit as a missing protection.
The memo recommends adding a joint ITAR/export compliance protocol exhibit consistent with the playbook and VDS standard form.
The memo says the draft's exclusivity deviates from the preliminary understanding of mutual exclusivity limited to the JTCP solicitation only.
The memo highlights that exclusivity deviation as negotiation leverage.
The memo says the draft's non-binding workshare deviates from the preliminary understanding that 28% workshare was discussed as a binding commitment.
The memo highlights that workshare deviation as negotiation leverage.

The memo says the draft's perpetual/irrevocable background IP license deviates from the preliminary understanding that VDS would retain Spectra-Link background IP with only a limited performance license.
The memo says the draft's permissive 'may' subcontract language deviates from the preliminary understanding that subcontract issuance would be mandatory upon award.
The memo discusses VDS's small business status as negotiation leverage.
The memo discusses the solicitation's ≥35% small business subcontracting goal as negotiation leverage.
The memo says VDS's 28% workshare contributes significantly toward the ≥35% goal and strengthens VDS's negotiating position on the binding workshare commitment.
The memo assigns a risk rating to every identified deviation.
The memo uses High for walk-away or material financial/legal exposure items, Medium for significant deviations requiring negotiation, and Low for minor or cosmetic deviations.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 3 revising exclusivity to co-exclusive status.
The redline caps the no-award exclusivity tail at 6 months post-proposal submission.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 4 narrowing the non-compete to solicitation W15QKN-25-R-0412 only.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 5 replacing 'commercially reasonable efforts' with a binding 28% workshare commitment with ±3% tolerance.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 8 revising foreground IP to developing-party ownership with a performance-only license.

The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 8 replacing the perpetual/irrevocable background IP license with a limited, revocable license for proposal preparation and contract performance only.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 7 changing 'may' to 'shall'.
The redline adds a 60-day post-award deadline for the subcontract obligation.
The redline references a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 12 making termination for convenience mutual.
The redline extends the termination notice period to 30 days.
The redline adds B&P cost reimbursement.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 14 revising the liability cap from $250,000 to the greater of $2,000,000 or 2× task-order workshare value.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 13 making indemnification mutual and symmetrical.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 15 replacing binding arbitration with negotiation → mediation → litigation in E.D. Va.
The redline adds an injunctive relief carve-out.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 10 revising ITAR/export obligations to be mutual.
The redline references a joint compliance protocol exhibit.
The redline includes a new provision for mutual protest/award challenge cooperation for GAO or COFC protests.
The redline adds VDS key personnel to Exhibit C or the key personnel provisions with consent-to-reassign protections.
The redline adds or references a new exhibit for pre-negotiated subcontract terms.
The redline adds or references a new exhibit for a joint ITAR compliance protocol.
The redline adds or references a new exhibit for VDS key personnel protections.
The memo identifies Article 8's phrase 'in connection with' the teaming arrangement as overbroad.
The memo says the phrase could sweep in pre-existing VDS developments and work outside the JTCP program.
The memo recommends narrowing the scope to IP developed solely in performance of the specific subcontract.
The memo says the 'in connection with' language risks capturing modifications or enhancements to Spectra-Link, which is used across multiple VDS programs.
The memo says VDS's Spectra-Link data qualifies as 'limited rights' technical data under DFARS 252.227-7013 and 'restricted rights' computer software under DFARS 252.227-7014.
The memo says the draft's perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free background IP license to Apex is inconsistent with these DFARS protections.
The redline markup of Article 8's background IP provisions references or incorporates DFARS 252.227-7013 and/or -7014 protections for VDS's limited rights/restricted rights data.
The memo is addressed to Nathaniel R. Chu, General Counsel, VDS.
The memo references engagement number LHR-2025-0743.
The memo references or is dated in relation to the July 18, 2025 deadline.
The memo says the mutual consequential damages waiver in Article 14 could prevent VDS from recovering lost profits if Apex fails to issue a binding subcontract or terminates.
The memo says the waiver puts the $45.27M workshare at risk.
The memo recommends either carving out lost workshare value from the waiver or tying it to the revised liability cap.
Each deviation in the memo identifies the specific article or section of the Apex draft.
Each deviation in the memo identifies the corresponding playbook requirement.
Each deviation in the memo describes the nature of the deviation.
Each deviation in the memo includes a High, Medium, or Low risk rating.
Each deviation in the memo includes a recommended negotiation position and fallback options.
The memo flags that Article 7 states full flow-down 'without negotiation'.
The memo recommends pre-negotiated subcontract terms with appropriate tailoring.
The memo addresses the mixed FFP/CPFF task order structure of the IDIQ when discussing the pre-negotiated subcontract terms.
